entry_conditions: Use within the entire expanded finish_red support, including the shared blue-setdown-to-red-lift transition. Inputs are two causal states: qpos 0:9 and qvel 9:18 (including individual fingers), TCP pose 18:25, red pose 25:32, blue pose 32:39, red goal 41:44 and blue goal 44:47, with world metre positions and wxyz orientations. At early entry blue is close to TCP and held above blue_goal, fingers are about 0.01825 m each, and red is supported near [-0.181,0,0.020] m. Measured start TCP heights across the assigned data are about 0.138 to 0.209 m, not a hard entry threshold. Later valid entries include open-finger blue release/empty transit, open red approach and closed-finger red lift. The learned role encoder combines width, velocity, proximity and two-frame object/TCP co-motion; it does not require a stored predecessor transform or a preset phase index. Nearness alone is insufficient proof of attachment, especially before closure.
exit_conditions: The terminal task contract is red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal: goals near [-0.35,0.20,0.02] m and [-0.35,-0.20,0.02] m, full rotated block footprint inside the goal squares and the declared z tolerance. Exact center coincidence is unnecessary. Supported terminal continuation states have both blocks on the table, fingers near 0.04 m each and TCP near z=0.30 m; this opening/retreat is learned but is not an extra success predicate. At demo10111:966 red is [-0.35095,0.19525,0.02431] m while TCP is [-0.35941,0.19542,0.02433] m and the command remains closed. This illustrates both nonzero grasp offset and the distinction between geometric success and optional release completion. No additional speed or sustained-hold requirement is imposed.
overlap_role: The model is trained on all expanded actions, not only final red placement. In demo10100 the shared interval [600,850) includes blue descent and setdown, blue opening, empty rise/travel, red descent, new closure and lift; demo10111 shares [603,844). Across demonstrations the overlap contains 239 to 250 actions. The representation recomputes separate blue and red transforms from current observations and gates them with learned blue-attached/empty/red-attached probabilities. It learns to discount old-blue compensation after opening and use new-red geometry after closure/co-motion; it never transfers a persistent blue offset into the red grasp. Empty TCP-to-red features and absolute robot state support intervening travel, while both object goals remain visible.
successor_readiness: Pass current measured world TCP/object poses and goals, plus causal qpos/qvel/finger history, to the inference agent or any successor. Grasp-frame features and role probabilities are internal and need not be initialized or exported. A blue goal predicate may already hold at setdown while blue opening or red retrieval is unfinished, so do not interpret that single predicate as terminal readiness. If both predicates hold, terminal evaluation can complete immediately under the supplied contract. If further robot motion is desired, observed opening and separation of TCP from the settled blocks provide evidence for empty retreat rather than another grasp-relative placement correction. Contact and attachment remain inferred, not directly measured.
failure_signatures: Concerning behavior includes moving the TCP to the block-goal center while ignoring a measured nonzero object/TCP offset; retaining blue-conditioned compensation during empty travel or red lift; using the wrong wxyz rotation or world/tool axis convention; assuming contact before the fingers settle; and continuing a supposed rigid grasp when object/TCP motion disagrees. Failure may also appear as disturbing supported blue, regrasping an already valid red placement, or misclassifying final open retreat as red approach. These signatures are monitoring cues, not implemented recovery guarantees or hard action constraints. The learned forward-pose auxiliary is not a certified dynamics model.
continuation_guidance: Continue on fresh causal observations in the framework's short chunks while blue release, empty travel, red closure/lift or red placement remains incomplete. The complete slice also supports demonstrated final opening and withdrawal if the API elects to continue after task success. Fingers opening toward 0.04 m and a supported object whose motion no longer follows the rising TCP should reduce reliance on attachment compensation. Use qpos/qvel and TCP height/motion to distinguish approach, setdown and retreat rather than a global clock. Do not demand zero goal error or corrective centering after valid placement, and do not add opening, clearance or stability-hold conditions to task success. Transfer to terminal evaluation when both declared predicates hold; unsupported disturbances or failures should be reassessed by the inference agent rather than assumed recoverable by longer invocation.
limitations: Evidence concerns nearly upright rigid 0.04 m blocks, top-down grasps and the same fixed-base Panda controller. Observed offset and start/end variation are narrow. Two causal observations can support attachment inference but cannot prove grasp/contact or resolve every stationary dwell. Source-index examples and measured boundary statistics are training evidence, not inference inputs, a schedule or hard admissibility bounds. No performance feedback, yaw/offset perturbation evaluation, unseen-buffer recovery, analytic IK, image encoding, global SE(3) invariance or guaranteed object preservation is claimed. The sampler remains learned joint-action DDPM; geometric gating does not script actions.
